title: A2 Writing Quiz 3 — Sports, Recovery & Outdoor Fun

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She has already finished her medicine.
She has already finish her medicine.
She already has finished her medicine yet.
She has finished already her medicine.
questions.explanation: 'Already' usually comes between the auxiliary and past participle: 'has already finished'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have played football last Saturday.
We played football last Saturday.
We have play football last Saturday.
We are playing football last Saturday.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression ('last Saturday') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The sun was shining when we arrived at the beach.
The sun shone when we were arriving at the beach.
The sun was shine when we arrived at the beach.
The sun shining was when we arrived at the beach.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (main event): 'The sun was shining when we arrived.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This exercise is easyer than the last one.
This exercise is more easy than the last one.
This exercise is easier than the last one.
This exercise is easiest than the last one.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -ier: 'easier than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: January is the coldest month of the year here.
January is the more cold month of the year here.
January is the most coldest month of the year here.
January is coldest month of the year here.
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjective superlative: 'the coldest'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: My knee hurts, so I can't run today.
My knee hurts, so I can't running today.
My knee hurts, so I not can run today.
My knee hurts, so I can't to run today.
questions.explanation: 'Can't' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'can't run'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I had to stayed in bed all weekend.
I had to stay in bed all weekend.
I have to stay in bed all weekend ago.
I must to stay in bed all weekend.
questions.explanation: Past of 'have to' is 'had to' + base verb: 'had to stay'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It might snows later today.
It might snow later today.
It might to snow later today.
It mights snow later today.
questions.explanation: 'Might' + base verb expresses possibility: 'might snow'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: They aren't going to travel because of the storm.
They aren't going travel because of the storm.
They going to not travel because of the storm.
They aren't go to travel because of the storm.
questions.explanation: Negative 'going to': aren't/isn't + going to + base verb: 'aren't going to travel'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you drink enough water, you won't get thirsty.
If you will drink enough water, you won't get thirsty.
If you drink enough water, you don't get thirsty won't.
If you drank enough water, you won't get thirsty.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will/won't + base verb: 'If you drink..., you won't get thirsty.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He finished doing his exercises an hour ago.
He finished to do his exercises an hour ago.
He finished do his exercises an hour ago.
He finished did his exercises an hour ago.
questions.explanation: 'Finish' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'finished doing'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We promised visiting grandma this weekend.
We promised to visit grandma this weekend.
We promised visit grandma this weekend.
We promised for visit grandma this weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Promise' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'promised to visit'.

questions.question: There are ___ people at the park because the weather is nice.
options: much
a lot of
little
much of
questions.explanation: 'A lot of' is used with countable plural nouns in positive sentences: 'a lot of people.'

questions.question: Can I have ___ sugar in my tea, please?
options: a few
a little
many
few
questions.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable, and 'a little' means 'a small amount of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'even though'.
options: Even though he was sick, he went to work.
Even though he was sick, but he went to work.
He went to work, even though but he was sick.
Even though, he was sick he went to work.
questions.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a contrast clause and doesn't need 'but': 'Even though he was sick, he went to work.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I take vitamins so that I stay healthy.
I take vitamins so that stay healthy.
I take vitamins for so I stay healthy.
I take vitamins so that staying healthy.
questions.explanation: 'So that' + clause expresses purpose: 'so that I stay healthy.'

questions.question: We went hiking ___ the bad weather.
options: in spite of
despite of
although
because
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'in spite of the bad weather.'

questions.question: The clinic said the results will be ready ___ two days.
options: within
during
since
until
questions.explanation: 'Within' means 'in less than' a period of time: 'ready within two days.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I can't come today.")
options: He said that he can't come today.
He said that he couldn't come that day.
He said that he couldn't come today.
He said he can't came today.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'can't' shifts to 'couldn't' and 'today' often shifts to 'that day'.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a gym receptionist you don't know?
options: Hi mate,
Dear Sir/Madam,
Yo,
Hey buddy,
questions.explanation: 'Dear Sir/Madam,' is used when writing formally without knowing the recipient's name.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a formal email when you know the recipient's name?
options: Yours faithfully,
Yours sincerely,
Take care,
Bye,
questions.explanation: 'Yours sincerely,' matches 'Dear [Name],' when the recipient's name is known.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Let's go cycling if the weather clears up.
Let's to go cycling if the weather clears up.
Let's going cycling if the weather clears up.
Let's went cycling if the weather clears up.
questions.explanation: 'Let's' + base verb is used to make a suggestion: 'Let's go cycling...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the park.' and 'We play football in the park.'?
options: This is the park who we play football in.
This is the park where we play football.
This is the park which we play football.
This is the park what we play football.
questions.explanation: 'Where' is used for places in relative clauses: 'the park where we play football.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He often catches a cold in winter.
He catches often a cold in winter.
Often he catches a cold in winter always.
He catches a cold often in winter.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'He often catches a cold.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Can you tell me if the pool is open today?
Can you tell me is the pool open today?
Can you tell me if the pool is open today.
Can you tell me, if the pool is open today?
questions.explanation: Indirect yes/no questions use 'if' with normal word order and end with a question mark.

questions.question: My legs hurt because I ___ all afternoon.
options: walk
have walked
have been walking
walked
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes an ongoing action explaining a present result: 'have been walking'.

questions.question: That bicycle isn't mine, it's ___.
options: him
his
he's
his's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's his.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, drink water. Next, stretch. Finally, start exercising.
First drink water next stretch finally start exercising.
Finally drink water, first stretch, next start exercising.
Next first drink water, finally stretch start exercising.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Next,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every one of the runners ___ water during the race.
options: need
needs
needing
are needing
questions.explanation: 'Every one of' takes a singular verb: 'Every one of the runners needs...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You've never tried skiing, have you?
You've never tried skiing, haven't you?
You've never tried skiing, do you?
You've never tried skiing, hadn't you?
questions.explanation: 'Never' makes the statement negative in meaning, so a positive tag is used: 'have you?'
